items.title: Withdrawal tracker can mark a just-mined transfer as 'dropped' and return the funds, so the player is paid twice
items.scenario:
A queued test-USDT withdrawal of 1,000.00 is broadcast at nonce n. On a tracker pass, getTransactionReceipt(hash) returns 'not found' because the tx is still in the mempool, or because a load-balanced RPC node is behind. The tx is then mined in the next Arbitrum block (about 250 ms later), and getTransactionCount(from,'latest') returns n+1. track() sets the outbox row to the terminal 'dropped' status. WithdrawalBroadcasterService.track() then calls failWithdrawal(), which posts withdrawal_release (LOCKED -> AVAILABLE +1,000.00). The ERC-20 transfer is final on-chain, and the player gets 1,000.00 back in Available and can withdraw it again. Later passes never re-check, because 'dropped' short-circuits at line 209.
  EVIDENCE: chain-signer.service.ts:218-223 reads the receipt; when it is absent, lines 250-260 run `const latestNonce = await client.getTransactionCount({ address, blockTag: 'latest' }); if (latestNonce > row.nonce) { ... status: 'dropped' ... return { state: 'dropped' } }`. There is no second receipt lookup, and the nonce does not have to be consumed `confirmations` blocks deep. withdrawal-broadcaster.service.ts:213-218: any non-mined, non-pending state goes to `this.failWithdrawal(w.id, ... 'transaction dropped (nonce replaced)')`. withdrawals.service.ts:625-638 `fail()` then calls `release()`, which posts withdrawalReleaseLines (LOCKED -> AVAILABLE).
  ALSO REPORTED (chain): Withdrawal tracker can mark a mined transfer as 'dropped' and refund it, so the player gets paid twice — A withdrawal tx (nonce N) is pending. The tracker calls getTransactionReceipt, which returns not-found. The tx is mined in the next Arbitrum block (about 250 ms later), or a load-balanced RPC answers the receipt call from a lagging node. The following getTransactionCount('latest') returns N+1, so track() writes status 'dropped' (a terminal state). WithdrawalBroadcasterService.track then calls failWithdrawal('transaction dropped (nonce replaced)'), which posts withdrawal_release (LOCKED -> AVAILABLE). The player has received the test-USDT on-chain AND has the full amount back in Available. They
items.fix: Declare 'dropped' only when the nonce was consumed at least `confirmations` blocks deep (getTransactionCount at blockTag head - confirmations + 1) and a second getTransactionReceipt(hash), made after the nonce read, still returns nothing. Otherwise return 'pending'. Do not treat 'dropped' as terminal until that check holds.

items.title: Daily (KYC) withdrawal limit can be exceeded with concurrent requests
items.scenario:
A KYC level-1 player has a 2,000.00 daily limit and 5,000.00 Available. Two POST /withdrawals of 1,500.00 each, with different idempotency keys, are sent at the same moment. Each READ COMMITTED transaction runs the aggregate of today's withdrawals before the other has committed, sees 0.00 used, and passes. Both then reach ledger.post(), where the user_available row lock only serializes the balance check, and both succeed. 3,000.00 is locked for withdrawal on the same day, against a 2,000.00 limit.
  EVIDENCE: Lines 136-155: `const today = await tx.withdrawal.aggregate({ ... status: { in: COUNTS_TOWARDS_LIMIT } }) ... if (usedToday.plus(money(quote.amount)).gt(money(limit))) throw`. No per-user lock is taken before this check. The first per-user lock is the FOR UPDATE inside ledger.post() at line 217 (ledger.service.ts:71-75), which comes after the limit check. The idempotency row only conflicts when the key is the same.
  ALSO REPORTED (rg-compliance): KYC daily withdrawal limit can be exceeded with concurrent requests (aggregate read without a per-user lock) — A Level 1 player (limit 2,000.00/day, Available 5,000) gets two single-use step-up tokens from POST /auth/2fa/challenge, about 30 s apart (each is valid 5 min). The player then fires two POST /withdrawals at the same moment with different idempotency keys, each for 2,000. Under READ COMMITTED both transactions run the withdrawal.aggregate before either commits, so both see usedToday = 0 and both pass the limit. ledger.post's FOR UPDATE only serialises the balance check, which passes. Result: 4,000 withdrawn today against a 2,000 KYC limit.
items.fix: Serialize withdrawal requests per user before reading usage. For example, run `SELECT ... FROM ledger_accounts WHERE code = 'user:<id>:available' FOR UPDATE`, or take pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(userId)), at the top of the transaction, then aggregate today's withdrawals.

items.title: Real on-chain deposits are credited to Available without the RG deposit limit, self-exclusion or deposits_blocked checks
items.scenario:
A player has a 500.00 weekly deposit limit, or later self-excludes, or gets a 'deposits_blocked' restriction. Their HD deposit address is already assigned. They send 5,000.00 test-USDT to it. The watcher records it (CHAIN_CLEARING -> PENDING) and after 20 confirmations credits all of it to AVAILABLE, where it can be staked. Only the DEMO simulate endpoints call assertCanDeposit, so the RG deposit limit is never enforced on the real deposit path.
  EVIDENCE: Lines 140-153 call deposits.recordDetected() and lines 246-249 call deposits.credit() with no RG or restriction check. `grep assertCanDeposit` returns only deposits.service.ts:211 and demo-deposits.service.ts:43 (both DEMO). DEPOSIT_POLICY (auth/guards.ts:41-46) only guards the HTTP address route, not the watcher. RG usage('deposit') does count these deposits (responsible-gaming.service.ts:583), so the limit is measured but never applied.
  ALSO REPORTED (rg-compliance): On-chain deposits skip every deposit-side RG and compliance check (deposit limits, self-exclusion/break, deposits_blocked, geo) — A player calls GET /deposits/address once (the HD address is persistent per user), then sets a 100 USDT daily deposit limit, starts a cooling-off break, or an admin applies deposits_blocked, or the player is now in a restricted country. The player sends 5,000 test-USDT to the saved address. The watcher's recordDetected() and then reconcile() -> deposits.credit() moves the full 5,000 PENDING -> AVAILABLE after N confirmations. Once the break ends (or right away if only a limit was set) the player can enter pools with money that was over the limit.
  ALSO REPORTED (chain): On-chain deposits are credited without RG deposit limits, self-exclusion, deposits_blocked or the deposits.enabled kill switch — A player sets a 50 USDT daily deposit limit, self-excludes, or gets admin restriction deposits_blocked. Their deposit address was issued earlier and stays valid. They send 500 test-USDT to it. After 20 confirmations the watcher credits all 500 to Available. The same happens while ops have turned off feature flag deposits.enabled. The deposit limit (and the admin view's 'held for compliance') is never applied to real chain deposits, only to the DEMO simulate endpoints.
  ALSO REPORTED (tests): On-chain deposits skip every RG and restriction check, and no test covers that path — A player starts a 7d cooling-off, self-excludes, sets a 100 USDT/week deposit limit, or gets an admin deposits_blocked restriction. They already know their deposit address (GET /deposits/address now returns 403, but the address row stays). They send 5,000 test USDT on Arbitrum Sepolia. DepositChainWatcherService picks up the Transfer log (deposit-chain-watcher.service.ts:141 recordDetected, :248 credit), and credit() posts deposit_credited to user_available. The full 5,000 lands in Available despite the exclusion or limit. docs/API.md:100 and :257 say breaks, self-exclusion and the deposits_bl
items.fix: In credit(), evaluate the deposit limit, self-exclusion and deposits_blocked for the user. Post the amount that exceeds the limit, or the whole amount for blocked or excluded users, to a withdraw-only bucket (e.g. OWED or a held account) instead of AVAILABLE, and notify the user. On-chain funds cannot be refused, but they must not become stakeable.

items.title: Production boot accepts the committed .env.example placeholder secrets, so anyone can forge step-up tokens (2FA bypass) and admin access tokens
items.scenario:
Someone runs `docker compose --profile prod up` and adds only PRIVY_APP_ID/SECRET to .env. The api service loads .env.example as its required base env_file (docker-compose.yml:17-21). The prod override (lines 152-160) only sets NODE_ENV/PRIVY_MOCK, so JWT_ACCESS_SECRET, ADMIN_JWT_ACCESS_SECRET and TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY keep their public values (.env.example:37,42,48), and boot accepts them. (a) A thief holding a player's Privy session reads `id` from GET /me and `sessionId` from POST /auth/session (auth.controller.ts:74). They sign {sub,sid,purpose:'withdrawal',typ:'step_up',jti:new} with the public secret (aud 'step-up', iss 'globalpool-api'). POST /withdrawals with X-Step-Up-Token passes StepUpService.assert without any TOTP code. Purpose 'security_settings' works the same way and lets them disable 2FA. (b) A read-only auditor (audit.read) calls GET /admin/audit-logs. The `admin.login` rows carry actorId plus metadata.familyId (admin-auth.service.ts:130, returned raw at admin.service.ts:430). The auditor signs {sub:superAdminId,sid:familyId,typ:'admin_access'} with the public ADMIN_JWT_ACCESS_SECRET. authenticate() finds the live session and returns full Super Admin permissions.
  EVIDENCE: secret() only checks `min(32)` (env.ts:33-34, used at 69-75). TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY only checks its byte length (env.ts:80). The 'dev-only-change-me-…' values are 47-50 chars long, so they pass. Step-up tokens are signed and verified with JWT_ACCESS_SECRET (step-up.service.ts:47,71); assert() checks only sub/sid/purpose/typ and jti freshness (lines 85-103). env.spec.ts 'rejects weak secrets' only tests short strings. ARCHITECTURE.md says 'weak secrets … stop the process', but no placeholder or denylist check exists.
items.fix: When NODE_ENV=production, refuse to boot on any secret that matches the .env.example values or contains 'dev-only'/'change-me' (JWT_*, ADMIN_JWT_*, TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY, PRIVY_MOCK_SIGNING_SECRET). Stop loading .env.example in the prod compose profile. Use a dedicated STEP_UP_SECRET, and drop familyId from audit metadata (or hash it).

items.title: Self-exclusion and breaks end automatically, but the UI promises 'nothing reopens automatically' plus a 24 h cool-down and mandatory limits
items.scenario:
A player self-excludes for 6 months. At endsAt + 1 s, exclusion() no longer matches the row (endsAt > now is false), so assertNotSelfExcluded passes. POST /pool/rounds/:id/entries and POST /dev/deposits/simulate work again at once: no reopen request, no support review, no 24 h cool-down, no limits required. The RG7 screens and the restricted page told the player the account stays closed until they ask to reopen.
  EVIDENCE: responsible-gaming.service.ts:390-395 checks only `OR: [{ endsAt: null }, { endsAt: { gt: now } }]`, and :417-428 checks nothing else. The schema has no reopen state (prisma RgSelfExclusion has only startsAt/endsAt), and grep finds no reopen endpoint. The UI promises otherwise: rg-breaks.tsx:597 'When it ends, you must ask to reopen — nothing reopens automatically', :723 'reopening needs your request', :981 'Your account stays closed until you ask to reopen it', restricted.tsx:315 'Nothing switches back on automatically', :325-326 '24-hour cool-down, then limits first — You’ll set deposit and loss limits before you can play again'. Related: account-status.controller.ts:51/96-103 does not return the kind, so a 24 h cooling-off also lands on /restricted/self-excluded with the same 'ask support to reopen' copy.
items.fix: Make the server behave as promised for long durations: after endsAt, keep the account excluded until the player explicitly asks to reopen. Then apply a 24 h cool-down and require deposit and loss limits before assertCanParticipate or assertCanDeposit pass. Alternatively, change the copy to match the real behaviour, but the owner must decide. Return the kind (cooling_off / self_exclusion) from /auth/account-status so a short break is not shown as a self-exclusion. OWNER POLICY: implement what the UI/Figma promises (protective): when a self-exclusion or break ends nothing reopens automatically; the player must actively request reopening, a 24 h cool-down applies, and RG limits must be reviewed — keep enforcement server-side.

items.title: Rounds hang in 'closed' forever (stakes never drawn or refunded) when RANDOMNESS_PROVIDER=chainlink and the round is not mirrored
items.scenario:
(a) A production deploy must use RANDOMNESS_PROVIDER=chainlink because mock is refused in production. Env validation accepts it with POOL_ONCHAIN_MIRROR=false. (b) With the mirror on, a round can be left un-adopted: it was already closed, or within 60 s of closing, when the mirror was enabled, or it was created with a window under 60 s. In both cases startDraw takes the non-mirrored branch and calls randomness.request. Nobody sent requestDraw on-chain, so ChainlinkVrfProvider.request throws RandomnessNotReadyError on every 30 s tick. The round stays 'closed' with players' stakes locked indefinitely. There is no VRF-timeout cancel, because that only exists for 'drawing' rounds, and the error is not even logged.
  EVIDENCE: round-lifecycle.service.ts:192-196: `} else if (!round.thresholdsMet ...) {...} await this.randomness.request(round);`. chainlink-vrf.provider.ts:68-71 throws when there is no DrawRequested event. round-lifecycle.service.ts:88-89 deliberately skips logging RandomnessNotReadyError. env.ts:225-234 only checks mirror -> chainlink, never chainlink -> mirror. round-mirror.service.ts:314-322 and the 669 filter refuse adoption within 60 s of close.
items.fix: Add the reverse cross-field rule (RANDOMNESS_PROVIDER=chainlink requires POOL_ONCHAIN_MIRROR=true). In startDraw, cancel and refund, or alert, any round that is not mirrored while the Chainlink provider is active, instead of retrying forever. Log RandomnessNotReadyError after N ticks.

items.title: Core-flow CTAs and required documents link to routes that do not exist (404): the KYC step in withdraw, the onboarding consent documents, bonus terms, support from failed or delayed deposits, restricted countries
items.scenario:
(1) A player whose withdrawal precheck returns kyc_required clicks the only CTA, 'Verify identity', and gets 404 'Page not found'; the real page is /account/kyc or /account/kyc/verify. (2) Onboarding requires ticking 'I accept the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy', but both links open 404s, so consent is recorded for documents the player cannot read; the KYC flow's /legal/aml and /legal/privacy links are also 404. (3) The sign-up dialog's welcome offer '100% up to 500 USDT · 30× wagering · Terms apply' links to /promotions (404), so the bonus terms cannot be read. (4) A delayed or failed deposit says 'contact support with reference …' and links to /support (404); there are 18 /support links in total, including those on the restricted and blocked pages. (5) The restricted-region banner and the restricted pages link to /legal/restricted-countries (404). The pool licence card links to /legal/licence (404).
  EVIDENCE: There is no page.tsx for /account/verification, /legal/*, /support or /promotions under apps/web/src/app (next.config.ts has no rewrites, and app/not-found.tsx renders 'Page not found'). Links: withdraw-flow.tsx:1086; auth/onboarding.tsx:349 and 356; account/kyc-flow/flow.tsx:895 and 898; auth/auth-dialog.tsx:223; auth/auth-ui.tsx:666; wallet/deposit-flow.tsx:931, 1097 and 1479; auth/restricted.tsx:170, 251, 339, 438 and 699; shell/app-shell.tsx:125; pool/parts.tsx:39 (POOL_ROUTES.restricted) and 297.
items.fix: Point the KYC CTA at ACCOUNT_ROUTES.kycVerify ('/account/kyc/verify'). Add at least placeholder /legal/{terms,privacy,aml,aml-kyc,restricted-countries,licence,fees,cookies}, /support and /promotions pages; DEMO copy is acceptable, but the consent targets must render. Or remove the links and the bonus card until those pages exist.

items.title: RG participation limit subtracts refunds of purchases from earlier periods, so the player can stake beyond the limit
items.scenario:
A player has a 100.00 daily participation limit. Yesterday they bought 9 entries (90.45 USDT). That round is cancelled today, and a 90.00 'refund' transaction is created today. Today usage = Σ entry_purchase(today) − Σ refund(today) = 0 − 90.00, clamped to 0. The player can now buy entries until today's purchases minus 90.00 reach 100.00, which is about 190 USDT staked in one day under a 100.00 limit. A weekly or monthly limit is bypassed the same way when a round is cancelled at the start of the period.
  EVIDENCE: Lines 584-588: `const spent = (await this.sumOf(db, userId, 'entry_purchase', since)).minus(await this.sumOf(db, userId, 'refund', since)); if (type === 'participation') return toUSDTString(maxZero(spent));`. sumOf filters on `createdAt: { gte: since }` (line 609). Refund transactions are created at cancel time (round-lifecycle.service.ts:481-500), and nothing links them to the purchase's period.
items.fix: Only net refunds whose original purchase falls in the current period. For example, sum refunds joined to entry_purchase transactions of the same round that were created since `since`, or exclude stakes of cancelled rounds by purchase date instead of subtracting refund rows by refund date.

items.title: Deposit watcher drops a second identical Transfer to the same address in one transaction, so it is never credited
items.scenario:
One on-chain transaction, for example an exchange batch payout or a multisend, emits two Transfer logs of 100.00 test-USDT to the same deposit address (logIndex 3 and 5). Log 3 is recorded as DP-x. For log 5, the 'known' lookup finds DP-x (same txHash, toAddress and amount, and logIndex 3 ≠ 5), so it is treated as a moved log and skipped. The user receives 200.00 on-chain but only 100.00 is credited, and reconcile() keeps matching DP-x to log 3.
  EVIDENCE: Lines 129-139: `const known = await this.prisma.deposit.findFirst({ where: { network, txHash: log.transactionHash, toAddress: to, amount, logIndex: { not: log.logIndex ?? 0 } } }); if (known) continue;`.
  ALSO REPORTED (chain): Deposit dedupe by (txHash, to, amount) silently drops legitimate transfers — (a) One tx, e.g. a batch or multisend contract or a smart-wallet multicall, sends 50 test-USDT twice to the same deposit address (logIndex 4 and 5). The first is recorded. For the second, the 'known' query finds the first row (same txHash, to, amount, different logIndex) and skips it, so only 50 of 100 USDT is ever credited. (b) A deposit is reversed as 're-orged out' (status rejected) and its tx is re-mined later. The scan's 'known' check matches the rejected row, or createMany hits the unique key, so the re-included transfer is never credited. In both cases the funds sit at the user's deposi
items.fix: Treat a log as a moved copy only when no Transfer with the recorded deposit's logIndex still exists in the current receipt, for example by matching through the receipt. Otherwise record each distinct (txHash, logIndex) as its own deposit.

items.title: A reversed (re-orged) deposit that is later re-included on-chain is never credited
items.scenario:
A 250.00 deposit is detected. Its block is re-orged out and the receipt stays missing for 20 blocks, which on Arbitrum is about 5 s, shorter than one 15 s poll. reverse() sets status 'rejected' and posts PENDING -> CHAIN_CLEARING. The tx is then re-included, either at the same logIndex or a new one. The rescan of the last N blocks finds the log again, but the deposit is never re-recorded: a same-logIndex log is blocked by createMany skipDuplicates on the (network, txHash, logIndex) unique key, and a new-logIndex log is blocked by the 'known' lookup at 129-139, which has no status filter and finds the rejected row. reconcile() only looks at detected/confirming rows, so the funds sit in custody and are never credited.
  EVIDENCE: reverse() at lines 298-304 sets `status: 'rejected'`. deposits.service.ts:90-112 `createMany(..., skipDuplicates: true); if (inserted.count === 0) return null;`. The 'known' query at watcher:129-139 has no `status` condition. reconcile() at line 185 uses `status: { in: ['detected', 'confirming'] }`.
items.fix: When a rejected deposit's (txHash, logIndex) or matching transfer reappears in a canonical receipt, reopen it: set it back to confirming, post deposit_detected again with a new event key, and let the normal credit path run. Exclude rejected rows from the 'known' lookup.

items.title: Entry history shows the whole round's refund and prize on every purchase row of that round
items.scenario:
A player buys 35 entries and then 10 more in round #1,245, which is cancelled. GET /history/entries returns one row per purchase. Each row reports refund = 10.00 × 45 = 450.00, so the list and CSV (apps/web/src/components/pool/entries-page.tsx:94-95) show 900.00 refunded where 450.00 is owed. If the player wins with one entry, both purchase rows show kind 'won' with the full prize and the same winningEntryIds.
  EVIDENCE: Rows are entry_purchase transactions (lines 61-73). `refunds = refundEntries.filter((g) => g.roundId === round.id)` and `mine = winners.filter((w) => w.roundId === round.id)` are per round, not per transaction. The refund is computed as `usdt(price.times(kind === 'refund_owed' ? owed || entries : back))`, where `owed` and `back` count the user's entries across the whole round.
items.fix: Scope refund and win results to the purchase: count refund_owed/refunded entries and winners whose entry.transactionId equals t.id (entries carry transactionId, entries.service.ts:128), or use `entries` from this purchase's metadata for the refund.

items.title: TOTP step-up and admin-login lockout counters are stale read-modify-write: concurrent guesses bypass the 5-attempt lock and can even clear an active lock
items.scenario:
An attacker holds a stolen player session and sends 120 parallel wrong codes to POST /auth/2fa/challenge (the per-IP default throttle allows this). Every request loads the row while failedAttempts=0 (verifyActive: find at line 133), so every request writes failedAttempts=1 and lockedUntil=null. 120 guesses cost 1 counted failure instead of locking after 5. The lock only lands after about 5 such bursts, so roughly 600 guesses per lock window per IP versus the intended 5. A slow request still in flight (stale count 3) writes lockedUntil=null and wipes a lock that a parallel request just set. The admin login has the same pattern for password and TOTP guesses (admin-auth.service.ts:85-97).
  EVIDENCE: totp.service.ts:198-203: `const failed = row.failedAttempts + 1; … update({ data: { failedAttempts: lockedUntil ? 0 : failed, lockedUntil } })`. It uses the row read before the async verify, with no row lock or atomic increment, and writes lockedUntil=null on every non-final failure. admin-auth.service.ts:85-93: `attempts = admin.failedLoginAttempts + 1` and `lockedUntil: lock ? … : admin.lockedUntil` (the stale null overwrites a concurrent lock).
items.fix: Do the increment atomically in SQL (`UPDATE … SET failed_attempts = failed_attempts + 1 … RETURNING failed_attempts`). Set locked_until in the same statement when the threshold is reached, and never write locked_until=NULL on a failed attempt. Alternatively, SELECT … FOR UPDATE inside a transaction.

items.title: Four-eyes inbox and approval detail are gated only by dashboard.read, exposing AML holds, suspensions and flagged withdrawals to roles without users/withdrawals/aml permissions
items.scenario:
The Marketing Lead role has dashboard.read but no users.read, withdrawals.read or aml.read (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:469-477). They call GET /admin/approvals/inbox?view=open, then GET /admin/approvals/:id. The response contains every pending 'user.restriction.apply' request: the player's handle and publicId, the restriction type (withdrawals_frozen / account_suspended) and the compliance officer's free-text requestReason. It also contains flagged-withdrawal releases (reference, amount, withdrawal id) and the full audit trail of reasons. The equivalent list GET /admin/approvals requires withdrawals.read (admin.controller.ts:224).
  EVIDENCE: admin-console.controller.ts:51-52 and 61-62 use `@RequirePermissions('dashboard.read')` only. FourEyesService.view() returns requestReason, decisionReason and the full payload (four-eyes.service.ts:721-727). detail() adds the auditTrail with reasons (lines 256-285). inbox() never filters items by whether the viewer may see the target module. The e2e tests only exercise super_admin viewers.
items.fix: Filter inbox and detail items to actions whose module permission the viewer holds (withdrawal.approve: withdrawals.read; user.restriction.apply: users.read; admin role changes: system.read). Alternatively require those permissions on the routes, and redact requestReason/payload for non-eligible viewers.

items.title: Admin 15-minute idle timeout exists only in the browser; the server refreshes an idle admin session for the full 8 h
items.scenario:
An admin closes the console tab, or the tab is discarded before the client idle timer runs endSession, which is what revokes the family through logout. Hours later someone at the machine uses 'Reopen closed tab' (Chrome restores sessionStorage with the refresh token), or anyone who obtained the refresh token, and calls POST /admin/auth/refresh. Refresh succeeds until the absolute ADMIN_SESSION_TTL (8 h), with no password or TOTP. On reload the web resets lastActivity to now after the refresh, so the console opens signed in even though the UI promises sign-out after 15 minutes idle.
  EVIDENCE: refresh() checks only rotatedAt, revokedAt and expiresAt (admin-auth.service.ts:136-163). No last-activity or idle check exists, and authenticate() checks none either. The idle limit is a web constant: session.tsx:29 `ADMIN_IDLE_MINUTES = 15`, enforced client-side at :204. The restore path (session.tsx:211-234) calls refresh() and then sets `lastActivity.current = Date.now()`.
items.fix: Store last_seen_at on the admin session and reject refresh or access when now − last_seen_at exceeds the idle limit (15 min), revoking the family. Update last_seen_at in authenticate(), throttled.

items.title: Admin login page redirects to an unsanitized ?next= when a session is restored (open redirect / javascript: URL in the admin origin)
items.scenario:
An admin tab already holds a session: its refresh token is in sessionStorage, which survives cross-origin navigation within the tab. That tab gets navigated to /admin/login?next=https://evil.example/admin/login, for example by an external page the admin opened in the same tab. The effect immediately runs router.replace(next). Next 15.5 treats a cross-origin href as external and calls location.replace, so the admin lands on a clone that asks for password + TOTP again. With next=javascript:… the same location.replace path runs script in the admin origin, which can read the refresh token from sessionStorage.
  EVIDENCE: login.tsx:244-246: `if (session.status === 'signed_in' && !previewState) router.replace(params.get('next') ?? '/admin');` has no validation. The post-login branch at :261 does check `next.startsWith('/admin')`, and other pages use safeNext(). The installed Next 15.5.29 app-router sends external URLs to `location.replace(canonicalUrl)` (node_modules/next/dist/client/components/app-router.js:84,277) and has no javascript: filter.
items.fix: Apply the same check as line 261 (`safeNext(raw)` and require the '/admin' prefix) before router.replace in the already-signed-in effect.

items.title: Rounds already committed on-chain fall back to the DB-only draw/cancel path when POOL_ONCHAIN_MIRROR is turned off (VRF-timeout refund of an owed draw, or a mock re-roll in non-prod)
items.scenario:
Round #N has chainMirror=true. Its entries are committed and requestDraw has been sent to GlobalPoolRounds (on-chain status DrawRequested). The operator then restarts the API with POOL_ONCHAIN_MIRROR=false, which env validation allows. (a) With RANDOMNESS_PROVIDER=chainlink (production): if VRF is still unfulfilled after VRF_TIMEOUT_HOURS, the non-mirrored branch marks the request timed_out and cancels the round with reason 'vrf_timeout', refunding every stake to Owed. The contract never cancels a requested draw, so it later stores the VRF word and computeWinners() returns 13 winners. The DB says refunded, the on-chain attestation says drawn, and nothing ever reconciles the two. (b) With RANDOMNESS_PROVIDER=mock (any non-production env): if the round is still 'closed', startDraw creates a new mock request whose word comes from a server-generated UUID. settle() then credits winners from that word without verifyDraw. The DB winners differ from the contract's winners for the real VRF word, so flipping config re-rolls the draw.
  EVIDENCE: mirrored() returns `round.chainMirror && this.mirror.enabled` (lines 66-68), so a per-round on-chain commitment is overridden by a process-wide env flag. Non-mirrored branches: startDraw lines 192-196 (randomness.request with whatever provider is configured) and pollAndSettle lines 267-273 (timeout -> cancel(roundId,'vrf_timeout')). settle() (line 282) has no mirror check of its own; verifyDraw is only called from the mirrored branch at line 220. config/env.ts:225-233 only validates the mirror=true -> chainlink direction. round-mirror.service.ts sync() (643-660) only re-mirrors cancellations with cancelReason 'threshold_not_met', never 'vrf_timeout'. ARCHITECTURE.md states 'a requested draw is never cancelled'.
items.fix: Decide per round from round.chainMirror and do not consult the env flag for rounds already adopted. If chainMirror is true but the mirror is disabled or misconfigured, refuse to draw, cancel or settle and raise an alert. Never apply the VRF-timeout cancellation, or a non-chainlink provider, to a chainMirror round.

items.title: Second withdrawal approval overwrites a concurrently withdrawn first approval (no status guard), releasing a flagged withdrawal
items.scenario:
Flagged WD-77 is under_review, and Admin A has given the first approval (pending row P). A calls POST /admin/approvals/P/withdraw to revoke it. At the same moment Admin B calls POST /admin/withdrawals/WD-77/approve. B's transaction locks the withdrawal row and reads P as pending (findFirst). A's withdraw does not lock the withdrawal row, so its updateMany(status pending -> cancelled) commits. B then runs tx.adminApproval.update({where:{id:P}}), which matches by id only and turns 'cancelled' back into 'approved'. The withdrawal moves to queued and is broadcast, although the only standing consent at execution time was B's. The audit log shows 'approval.withdrawn' followed by 'withdrawal.approve'.
  EVIDENCE: withdrawals.service.ts:388-395 reads the pending approval. Lines 428-442 check the requester, then `tx.adminApproval.update({ where: { id: pending.id }, data: { status: 'approved', ... } })` runs with no `status: 'pending'` predicate and no count check. four-eyes.service.ts:406-421 withdraw() runs its own transaction with only the approval-row CAS and never takes the withdrawal row lock that adminApprove relies on.
items.fix: Claim the approval with `updateMany({ where: { id: pending.id, status: 'pending' } })` and abort with CONFLICT unless count === 1. Alternatively, have withdraw() and reject() take the same withdrawal row lock (or lock the approval row FOR UPDATE) before changing a withdrawal approval.

items.title: Four-eyes first approvals for flagged withdrawals never expire (no expiresAt), so a stale approval can be completed weeks later
items.scenario:
Admin A gives the first approval on flagged WD-12 on 1 Nov. The withdrawal sits in under_review. On 25 Nov (new AML context, A has since left the team) Admin B approves and the withdrawal is queued and broadcast on A's 24-day-old approval. Restriction and role-change requests created through FourEyesService.request expire after FOUR_EYES_EXPIRY_HOURS (4 h) and 'then change nothing'. Withdrawal approvals, the money-moving four-eyes action, are exempt. The inbox shows them with expiresAt null, sorted last, as permanently open.
  EVIDENCE: adminApprove creates the row with `payload: { reference, amount }` only (lines 397-406), with no expiresAt. four-eyes.service.ts expiresAtOf() returns null when payload.expiresAt is missing (62-65), and expireStale skips such rows: `if (!exp || exp > now) continue;` (454-455), although 'withdrawal.approve' is an own action. The second approval (withdrawals.service.ts:387-443) never checks the age of the pending row. FourEyesService docs (lines 67-71) and API.md 'Requests expire after FOUR_EYES_EXPIRY_HOURS (4) and then change nothing'.
items.fix: Set payload.expiresAt = createdAt + FOUR_EYES_EXPIRY_HOURS when adminApprove creates the first approval. In the second-approval path, treat a pending row past its expiry as expired: mark it expired with a system audit row, and start a new first approval instead of completing it.

items.title: VRF event scans default to the last 50,000 blocks (about 3.5 h on Arbitrum Sepolia), so a missed DrawFulfilled leaves the round in 'drawing' forever
items.scenario:
POOL_CONTRACT_START_BLOCK is unset (.env.example ships it empty, and empty strings are treated as unset). VRF fulfils round #N's draw, but the rounds worker is down, or getLogs keeps failing, for more than about 3.5 h (50k blocks at roughly 0.25 s each). When polling resumes, fulfillment() scans only [head-50k, latest], finds no DrawFulfilled and returns null. In the mirrored branch, drawAttempts is not greater than known, and canReRequest() is false because the on-chain status is Fulfilled. pollAndSettle therefore returns 'waiting' on every tick and the 13 prizes are never credited, although the word is sitting in contract storage. The same window applies to request(): a DrawRequested older than the window throws RandomnessNotReadyError, and the round stays 'closed'.
  EVIDENCE: fromBlock(): `return head > 50_000n ? head - 50_000n : 0n;` when cfg.fromBlock is undefined (52-56), used by request() (60-67) and fulfillment() (93-99, `const log = logs[0]`). env.ts:150 makes POOL_CONTRACT_START_BLOCK optional, and env.ts:205 turns '' into unset. round-mirror.service.ts canReRequest() returns false unless the status is DrawRequested (516). verifyDraw already reads state.randomWord from getRound, so the value is available without logs.
  ALSO REPORTED (chain): VRF fulfilment is only read from logs in a 50k-block window, so a late poll leaves a mirrored round stuck in 'drawing' — POOL_CONTRACT_START_BLOCK is optional and is empty in .env.example. DrawFulfilled is emitted, but the jobs process or RPC is down for longer than about 50,000 Arbitrum Sepolia blocks (a few hours). After that, fulfillment() scans only head-50k..latest, never sees the event and returns null forever. For a mirrored round, pollAndSettle never cancels, and canReRequest() is false because the on-chain status is Fulfilled. The round never settles and the prizes are never credited. If the start block is set instead, the getLogs range grows without bound (millions of blocks) and range-limited RPC prov
items.fix: Require POOL_CONTRACT_START_BLOCK when RANDOMNESS_PROVIDER=chainlink, or persist a per-round scan cursor. Better: once the contract is Fulfilled, read randomWord, fulfilledRequestId and fulfilledAt from getRound() rather than relying on a bounded log scan, and use logs only for the tx hash.

items.title: Ledger/audit integrity page reports append-only protection OK even when the triggers are disabled
items.scenario:
A DB owner runs `ALTER TABLE ledger_entries DISABLE TRIGGER ledger_entries_append_only;` (or disables the balanced-posting constraint trigger) and edits ledger rows. GET /admin/finance/ledger/integrity still returns appendOnly.ok = true with every trigger 'present', because a disabled trigger keeps its pg_trigger row. Admins see a green 'append-only enforced' state while UPDATE/DELETE is in fact allowed.
  EVIDENCE: `SELECT tgname FROM pg_trigger WHERE NOT tgisinternal AND tgname = ANY(...)` (847-848), then `ok: APPEND_ONLY_TRIGGERS.every((t) => present.has(t))` (856). tgenabled ('D' = disabled) is never read. APPEND_ONLY_TRIGGERS (32-40) also omits the *_no_truncate triggers and the entry_commitments / round_payouts append-only triggers from the onchain_mirror migration.
items.fix: Select tgenabled together with tgrelid::regclass, and report ok only when every expected trigger exists on the expected table with tgenabled IN ('O','A'). Add the *_no_truncate, entry_commitments and round_payouts triggers to the checked list.

items.title: Self-excluded players are told a second account can't be opened, but nothing links accounts
items.scenario:
A self-excluded player signs in through Privy with a different email (new DID). createUser makes a fresh account, onboarding asks only for consents, country and handle, and the new account can deposit (DEMO simulate or on-chain) and buy entries at once. The exclusion stays bound to the old userId only. The self-excluded page promised 'We check identity at sign-up, so a second account can’t be opened.'
  EVIDENCE: restricted.tsx:304-307 (copy). player-identity.service.ts:74-86 (createUser by DID only). auth.service.ts:28-91 onboard() has no identity, duplicate, wallet or device check. responsible-gaming.service.ts:417-418 assertNotSelfExcluded(userId) is per account. KYC is required only for withdrawals, and kyc-flow.service.ts has no duplicate-identity check (grep for duplicate/excluded finds nothing).
items.fix: Either implement cross-account exclusion: match on KYC identity (name + DOB), linked wallet addresses and verified email at onboarding and KYC, and apply the existing exclusion. Or remove the claim from the page until that exists. Prefer making the promise true: refuse creating/onboarding an account whose verified email, linked wallet address or KYC identity matches an active self-exclusion (tests); if any part cannot be done now, make the copy truthful about what is linked.

items.title: DEPOSIT_POLICY on the whole deposits controller blocks deposit history and tracker for self-excluded or travelling players; wallet then hides pending deposits
items.scenario:
A player has a deposit at 3/12 confirmations and starts a cooling-off break (or travels to a restricted country). GET /deposits and GET /deposits/ref/DP-xxxx now return 403 SELF_EXCLUDED / GEO_RESTRICTED. On /wallet the 'In progress' card reads deposits.data as undefined after the error, filters it to [], and shows nothing pending although money is confirming. The deposit tracker page fails. For DEMO progressive deposits, POST /dev/deposits/:ref/confirmations is also blocked, so the funds stay in Pending (not withdrawable) for the whole break.
  EVIDENCE: deposits.controller.ts:24 applies @PlayerAuth(DEPOSIT_POLICY) (region + notSelfExcluded + deposits_blocked) at class level, so it also covers the read-only list (:41-45) and ref (:47-51) routes. Line 55 covers the DEMO advance route the same way. web components/wallet/overview.tsx:281-299: pendingDeposits = (deposits.data?.items ?? []) and loading only checks isPending. API.md:257-258: 'withdrawals and history stay available'. The RG break screen (rg-breaks.tsx:551) promises 'Pending deposits · withdrawable once confirmed'.
items.fix: Keep DEPOSIT_POLICY only on GET /deposits/address and POST /dev/deposits/simulate. Use the default onboarded-only policy for the list, ref and confirmation-advance routes. Have the wallet card show an error state instead of treating a failed query as 'nothing in progress'.

items.title: Long self-exclusion is impossible in the web for a 2FA player without their authenticator (backup codes rejected, lockout blocks it)
items.scenario:
A player with 2FA on has lost their phone and wants a 1-year self-exclusion. The RG7 form accepts only a 6-digit code (maxLength 6, ready requires /^\d{6}$/). Even through the API, a backup code such as ABCD-1234 in totpCode fails selfExclusionSchema validation (400). After 5 wrong attempts STEP_UP_LOCKED blocks self-exclusion for 15 min. The web never offers the /auth/2fa/challenge step-up token route, the only one that takes backup codes. The documented step is 'TOTP when 2FA is on'; refusing the player's own backup codes is an extra barrier to self-exclusion.
  EVIDENCE: schemas/rg.ts:95 totpCode: totpCodeSchema.optional(), with schemas/auth.ts:22-27 totpCodeSchema = 6 digits only. responsible-gaming.service.ts:354-358 calls stepUp.assert('security_settings'). web rg-breaks.tsx:627-631 (ready requires /^\d{6}$/), :777-786 (Input maxLength 6, '6-digit code'), :647-649 (STEP_UP errors only shown on the field). totp.service.ts verifyRow throws STEP_UP_LOCKED while lockedUntil > now.
items.fix: Accept backup codes for self-exclusion: z.union([totpCodeSchema, backupCodeSchema]) and allow them in the web field, or open the existing step-up dialog that supports backup codes. When 2FA cannot be completed, consider allowing self-exclusion anyway, since it only restricts the account.

items.title: RG deposit limit can be exceeded with parallel DEMO deposit simulations (no per-user lock around the usage check)
items.scenario:
A player has a 100 USDT daily deposit limit and 0 used. Two POST /dev/deposits/simulate requests for 100 each, with different idempotency keys, run at the same time. Each transaction's assertCanDeposit sums the transaction table (0 used) before the other commits, so both pass and 200 is credited against a 100 limit. This is the only deposit path that enforces the limit in DEMO.
  EVIDENCE: deposits.service.ts:208-211 and demo-deposits.service.ts:40-43 call rg.assertCanDeposit(userId, amount, tx) inside idempotency.run. responsible-gaming.service.ts:554-573 is a plain aggregate (sumOf at :602-618) with no lock. idempotency.service.ts:34-40 serialises only identical keys. prisma.service.ts:39 uses ReadCommitted. Entries avoid this only because entries.service.ts:64 locks the round row.
items.fix: Lock per user before the usage aggregate, e.g. pg_advisory_xact_lock on the user id or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on rg settings/users, in assertCanDeposit. Use the same lock for assertCanParticipate so future game stakes in other tables or rounds cannot race either.

items.title: Homepage hero tells every visitor 'Threshold not met — entries refunded to Owed' between rounds
items.scenario:
With the default ROUND_AUTO_SCHEDULE=true, the tick schedules round N+1 as soon as round N closes, so GET /pool/rounds/current returns the scheduled round (open → scheduled → latest). fetchPoolSnapshot sets current = null and last = the scheduled round. DrawCard's !round branch then shows 'Round #N+1 · scheduled', 0.00, and the caption 'Threshold not met — entries refunded to Owed' (anything not 'settled' gets that caption) from about 20:00 to 08:00 UTC every day. This happens even when round N met its thresholds and is drawing or settled with winners.
  EVIDENCE: queries.ts:66-68 (current: open ? round : null, last: round). hero.tsx:653-674: caption = last.status === 'settled' ? ... : 'Threshold not met — entries refunded to Owed'. round-lifecycle.service.ts:136-146 auto-schedules when no open or scheduled round exists. rounds.service.ts:80-95 prefers the scheduled round. env.ts:194 ROUND_AUTO_SCHEDULE default true.
items.fix: Keep the previous closed, drawing or settled round as `last`, e.g. fetch /pool/rounds?status=closed,drawing,settled,cancelled&pageSize=1 or have the API return both. Derive the caption from the real status: 'cancelled' → refund copy, 'drawing' → 'Drawing', 'settled' → winners.

items.title: Deposit watcher never verifies eth_chainId, so a mainnet RPC URL makes real-money deposits creditable
items.scenario:
An operator sets ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL to an Arbitrum One endpoint (chain 42161) and TEST_USDT_ADDRESS_ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA to the mainnet USDT contract. Env validation passes because it only checks URL and address format. The withdrawal and round signers refuse (they check chainId), but the deposit watcher scans mainnet USDT Transfer logs to the derived deposit addresses (valid on every EVM chain) and credits real USDT into DEMO balances. Real money enters the platform with no way out through the signer.
  EVIDENCE: blockchain.service.ts:21-36 builds the viem client from the URL with no getChainId check. deposit-chain-watcher.service.ts:71-77 uses `this.blockchain.client(network)` directly and goes straight to getBlockNumber and getLogs. The only eth_chainId check is in ChainSignerService.client() (chain-signer.service.ts:93-111), which the watcher does not use. RandomnessService (randomness.service.ts:24) passes the same unchecked client to ChainlinkVrfProvider.
items.fix: Move the eth_chainId === EVM_CHAIN_ID check into BlockchainService.client(), or a shared verifiedClient(), and use it in the watcher and the VRF provider. Fail closed (skip, raise an alert) on mismatch. Optionally check at boot that the token contract's chain matches.

items.title: The 24 h VRF re-request (contract plus automatic keeper) lets the VRF operator choose between two outcomes
items.scenario:
A VRF node operator, or anyone able to delay fulfilment, knows request A's output once A's block is final. If A's winners are unwanted, A is withheld. After 24 h the platform keeper automatically calls requestDraw again (request B). The operator can now compute both outputs and fulfil whichever is preferred first. The contract accepts the first fulfilment of either request. This is the 'withhold and re-request' re-roll that Chainlink's VRF security guidance warns against.
  EVIDENCE: GlobalPoolRounds.sol:407-409 allows requestDraw again from DrawRequested once 24 h have passed, and keeps the old request valid (_requestToRound is never cleared). Lines 459-471 store the first DrawFulfilled for any request of the round. round-lifecycle.service.ts:243-264 issues the re-request automatically (`this.mirror.requestDraw(round, { knownAttempts: known })`). chainlink-vrf.provider.ts:89-97 accepts whichever request fulfilled first.
items.fix: Do not re-request randomness. On VRF timeout, cancel the committed round with refunds (new on-chain reason, e.g. VRF_TIMEOUT, allowed only from DrawRequested after the timeout). Alternatively, invalidate the earlier requestId when re-requesting so only the latest request can fulfil, and gate re-requests behind the admin multisig with an audit row. Follow Chainlink VRF security guidance (never re-request randomness): on VRF timeout the round is cancelled and every stake refunded instead of re-requesting; update the contract (unaudited, not deployed), its tests, the API mirror/keeper, docs/CONTRACTS.md and the GP-13 copy.

items.title: A re-org that shifts log indices can collide with a sibling deposit's unique key and halt the whole watcher
items.scenario:
Tx T pays two platform deposit addresses: X at logIndex 7 and Y at logIndex 8. A re-org re-includes T one log later (X=8, Y=9). reconcile processes X first and runs deposit.update(logIndex: 8), which violates @@unique([network, txHash, logIndex]) held by Y. reconcile is not caught per row, so watch() returns 'skipped: reconcile failed' before scanning. The same row order repeats on every pass, so no deposit for any user is detected or credited until someone fixes the rows by hand.
  EVIDENCE: Lines 222-243 compute the new logIndex via matchTransfer and update it outside any conflict handling. Lines 84-87 abort the whole pass on any reconcile error. Rows are ordered only by blockNumber (line 190), so siblings in the same block come back in insertion order. The schema has @@unique([network, txHash, logIndex]) (schema.prisma:716).
items.fix: Re-index all deposits of the same txHash together in one transaction (e.g. move them to temporary negative indices first, or process them in descending order), and catch per-deposit errors so one bad row cannot stop the watcher.

items.title: Open redirect: safeNext() accepts '/<TAB>/host', which the browser turns into an external URL after sign-in and after the 2FA step-up
items.scenario:
An attacker sends a link like /2fa/challenge?purpose=withdrawal&next=/%09/evil.example/login. safeNext() lets '/\t/evil.example/login' through because the second character is a TAB, not '/' or '\'. When the player enters their TOTP code, or simply closes the dialog, StepUpPage.leave() calls window.location.assign(next). The WHATWG URL parser strips the TAB, so the target becomes //evil.example/login and the player lands on a phishing page right after proving their 2FA. The same value sent to /sign-in?next=... goes through AuthRouteOpener, which calls router.replace(next) at once for a visitor who is already signed in (no click needed). It also goes through SuccessView.proceed() (router.push(next)) after sign-in; the Next app router turns a cross-origin href into a full-page navigation.
  EVIDENCE: safe-next.ts:3 only rejects !raw.startsWith('/') || raw.startsWith('//') || raw.startsWith('/\\'). Checked with node: new URL('/\t/evil.com','http://localhost:3000').href === 'http://evil.com/', and the same happens with \n and \r\n. Sinks: components/auth/step-up.tsx:504 `const leave = () => window.location.assign(next ?? '/')`, which is called on verify (line ~539), cancel and Continue; app/(app)/2fa/challenge/page.tsx:24 passes the safeNext result straight in. components/auth/auth-route.tsx:30 `router.replace(next ?? '/')` runs for members. components/auth/auth-dialog.tsx:761 `router.push(next)`. Also onboarding.tsx:465 and two-factor-setup.tsx:224.
items.fix: Reject any control character or whitespace (/[\u0000-\u001F\u007F\s\\]/) and validate with new URL(raw, location.origin).origin === location.origin, then return the url's pathname+search+hash. Prefer router.replace over window.location.assign in StepUpPage.

items.title: Shell and homepage show hard-coded DEMO balance, entries, notifications and pool amount to every signed-in member, never their real data
items.scenario:
A member signs in (mock or Privy) with 0 USDT and deposits 100 test USDT. The /wallet page (GET /wallet/balances) shows 100.00 Available. On every page, the top bar pill, the mobile top bar and the drawer still show 'Available balance 9,215.30 USDT (demo)'. The sidebar shows 'My entries 35', the bell shows 3 notifications, the VIP tier shows gold, and the sidebar promo tile shows the DEMO round's pool amount. None of these ever change after a deposit, a withdrawal or buying entries. On the homepage in API mode, the hero tells the same member 'Your 35 entries · 351.75 USDT · ≈x% chance of any prize' with DEMO entry IDs, plus 'Available balance 9,215.30', for the real current round, even if they hold no entries.
  EVIDENCE: app-shell.tsx:26-35 DEMO_SHELL_MEMBER = { available: DEMO_BALANCES.available ('9215.30'), notifications: 3, activeEntries: DEMO_MY_ENTRIES.entries (35), vipTier:'gold', ... }. Lines 233-245 build member = { ...DEMO_SHELL_MEMBER, handle, initials } for every real user ('Until the API profile/balance endpoints exist' — /wallet/balances already exists and is used by walletApi.balances). Line 66: poolAmount = DEMO_CURRENT_ROUND.poolBalance. lib/data/queries.ts:108-121: myEntriesQuery and viewerBalanceQuery always mockResolve(...), even when DATA_SOURCE==='api'. These are consumed in components/home/home-page.tsx:50-51 and hero.tsx:217-224 and 751-772. The shell also hard-codes the restricted banner country: app-shell.tsx:130 '(United States)' whatever the real region is.
items.fix: Feed ShellMember from useBalances() (walletKeys.balances), the entries count from the pool my-entries API and the notification count from the notifications API, and feed poolAmount from the current-round query. Show skeletons while these load. Make myEntriesQuery and viewerBalanceQuery call the API in api mode, or hide those hero rows. Pass the real countryName into the restricted banner.

items.title: Player sign-out clears only ['auth'] queries; the next account in the same tab sees the previous player's wallet, account, RG and history data, including their anti-phishing code
items.scenario:
Player A uses /wallet/withdraw on a shared device and signs out; mock signOut and Privy logout() do not reload the page. Player B signs in on the same tab within 60 s and opens /wallet/withdraw. useMe() (['wallet','me'], staleTime 60 s, key not scoped by user) returns A's cached profile without refetching. The 'Withdrawal protections' card then shows A's anti-phishing code ('<code> — in every genuine email') and A's 2FA status. useBalances, useLinkedWallets (A's whitelisted addresses) and the transactions, KYC, devices, login-history and RG queries also render A's data until each one refetches. Disabled queries keep their data while the pages stay mounted, so nothing is garbage-collected.
  EVIDENCE: session-layer.tsx:139-142 clearAuthData() runs qc.removeQueries({ queryKey: authKeys.all }) only. Module caches live under ['wallet',…] (lib/api/wallet.ts:440-455), ['account',…] (lib/api/account.ts:526), ['rg'] and ['history'] (lib/api/rg-history.ts:95-116) and ['pool','me',…] (components/pool/use-pool.ts:39-41). None of these keys contains the user id; only authKeys.me includes the DID. mock-auth-provider.tsx:205-213 signOut only resets local state. The anti-phishing code is rendered at components/wallet/withdraw-flow.tsx:1414-1415.
items.fix: On signOut and on expire, call qc.clear() (or removeQueries for every player prefix: wallet, account, rg, history, pool/me, me), or include the user id in every player query key.

items.title: Deposit credited by the chain watcher jumps to 'Deposit credited' without refetching balances; the Before/After table shows the pre-credit Available
items.scenario:
A real (non-DEMO) deposit is detected, and PendingStep mounts useBalances() (Available 50.00, Pending 100.00). On Arbitrum Sepolia the watcher credits it a few seconds later. useDeposit's 4-second poll sees status 'credited', and the effect calls go('confirmation'). ConfirmationStep reads the same ['wallet','balances'] cache, which is still fresh under the 15 s staleTime, so it is not refetched. The page shows 'Deposit credited … moved from Pending to Available' while the table reads Available before -50.00, after 50.00 and Pending before 200.00, after 100.00. The background WalletOverview also keeps the old Available. Nothing triggers a refetch later: there is no interval and refetchOnWindowFocus is false.
  EVIDENCE: deposit-flow.tsx:194-196: the credited transition calls go('confirmation') without invalidating anything. lib/api/wallet.ts:412-423: useDeposit stops polling at credited and has no onSuccess invalidation. Only the DEMO paths invalidate: DemoSimulate (line 752) and DemoAdvance (line 1035). ConfirmationStep (lines 1109-1170) computes before = sub(b.available, deposit.amount) and after = b.available from the cached balances.
items.fix: In the effect at line 194, when status flips to 'credited', call invalidate() (walletKeys.all plus the other balance caches) before or alongside go('confirmation'). Have ConfirmationStep wait for balances.dataUpdatedAt to be newer than deposit.creditedAt.

items.title: The same balances, limits and history are cached under per-module keys, and financial and RG writes invalidate only their own module, so other screens act on stale Available balances and limits
items.scenario:
A player has 5.00 Available and 100.00 Owed and opens /pool, which caches ['pool','me','balances']. They claim the owed funds on /history/rewards; that claim invalidates only ['history']. They return to /pool within 15 s and open the participation modal. checkParticipation() uses the stale available '5.00', shows 'Not enough Available balance – you need 5.05 more', and disables Confirm even though the server holds 105.00. Similarly, after setting a lower participation limit or self-excluding on /responsible-gaming (which invalidates only ['rg']), the pool modal still shows 'Within your daily participation limit' from ['pool','me','rg']. After a withdrawal or cancel (['wallet'] only), the dashboard (['account','balances']) and history (['history','balances']) show the old Available. Entry purchases do not invalidate ['account'], ['history'] or ['rg'], so the RG 'used' meter stays at its old value.
  EVIDENCE: GET /wallet/balances is cached under walletKeys.balances, poolKeys.balances (use-pool.ts:39), accountKeys.balances (account.ts:530), historyKeys.balances (rg-history.ts:105) and authKeys.balances (auth/restricted.tsx:457). Invalidation scope: useInvalidateWallet (wallet.ts:498-501) covers ['wallet'] only and is used by withdraw, cancel, claim, whitelist and deposit; rg-history/finance.tsx:805 claim covers ['history'] only; useRgMutation (rg-history.ts:203-211) covers ['rg'] only; participate-flow.tsx:125-128 covers ['pool'], ['wallet'] and ['me'] but not account, history or rg. Defaults: staleTime 15_000, refetchOnWindowFocus false (app/providers.tsx). participate-flow.tsx:288-289: blocked = check.insufficient || check.limitReached.
items.fix: Use one shared balances/RG query key (for example ['player','balances'] and ['player','rg']) across modules, or add a single invalidatePlayerFinancials() that invalidates wallet, pool/me, account, history and rg, and call it from every financial or RG mutation.

items.title: Participation and withdrawal tell the player 'Nothing was charged' / 'wasn't requested' on transport errors where the outcome is unknown, which invites a duplicate purchase
items.scenario:
The player confirms 50 entries (502.50 USDT). The server commits the purchase but the response is lost (network drop, proxy 502/504, or a TypeError: Failed to fetch). The modal shows 'Your entries were not placed … Nothing was charged.' The player trusts this, changes the count to 40 and confirms. The intent key is replaced whenever the entry count changes, so the server books a second purchase. The withdraw 2FA step does the same: any error other than INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS or SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE shows 'The withdrawal wasn't requested' with an 'Edit withdrawal' button, even when the request may have been accepted.
  EVIDENCE: participate-flow.tsx:113-114: a new idempotency key is made whenever entries differ from the previous intent. Lines 306-326: the 'Your entries were not placed' callout with '{errorMessage(error)} Nothing was charged.' renders for every error, including non-ApiRequestError and 5xx. The key is kept only if the count stays the same. withdraw-flow.tsx:1168-1176 and 1209-1229: the 'other' error branch shows 'The withdrawal wasn't requested'.
items.fix: Only claim 'nothing was charged' for definite 4xx business errors. For network or 5xx errors, show 'We couldn't confirm — check My entries / Withdrawal history' and keep the same idempotency key, retrying the same intent until a definite answer arrives. Invalidate entries and balances so the real state is shown.

items.title: Participation modal says 'No participation limit set' while RG limits are still loading or failed to load
items.scenario:
A player with a 50 USDT/day participation limit opens /pool and clicks to buy entries before GET /responsible-gaming has returned, or after it failed. pool-hub passes limits={rg.data?.limits ?? null}. LimitCheck then renders the info callout 'No participation limit set – You can set a daily, weekly or monthly limit at any time' and no meter, which is false. The client-side limit check is also skipped, so the player confirms and only then gets RG_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
  EVIDENCE: components/pool/pool-hub.tsx:112 and 293: `limits={rg.data?.limits ?? null}`; the Participate button does not depend on rg.isPending or rg.isError (line 122). participate-flow.tsx:575-586: `if (!l && !details) return <Callout tone="info" title="No participation limit set">…`. logic.ts:76 loops over `input.limits ?? []`, so null means no limits.
items.fix: Pass the RG query state into ParticipateFlow. While pending, show a skeleton in LimitCheck; on error, show 'We couldn't load your limits — they are still enforced' instead of 'No participation limit set'. Disable Confirm until limits have loaded.

items.title: Admin sign-out and idle expiry remove only ['admin'] queries; ['admin-b'] (finance, pool, compliance data and the previous admin's /admin/auth/me) survives for the next admin
items.scenario:
Admin A (finance) is idle-logged-out on a shared workstation while on /admin/finance/withdrawals/WD-…. Admin B signs in within 60 s and opens the same withdrawal. useAdminMe() (['admin-b','me'], staleTime 60 s) returns A's cached profile. The four-eyes panel then reads 'First approver — you · <Admin A name>', and useCan() enables Approve/Reject affordances from A's permission list. The withdrawal queue, KYC/AML queues and ledger from A's session also render from cache until they refetch.
  EVIDENCE: session.tsx:144-154 clearLocal() runs queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: ['admin'] }). admin-b keys all start with 'admin-b' (lib/api/admin-b.ts:908-932), useAdminMe has staleTime 60_000 (lines 937-942) and useCan reads it (944-949). Consumed at admin-b/finance/withdrawal-detail-page.tsx:145-147 and 191, and admin-b/pool/control-pages.tsx:305-308. Related: ApprovalReviewDialog.refresh (admin-a/four-eyes.tsx:761-768) does not invalidate ['admin-b'], so the breaker and withdrawal pages stay stale after a four-eyes decision. 3 further lower-severity findings were left out: the shell restricted banner hard-codes 'United States' (app-shell.tsx:130); admin approvals 'Decided today' shows 'No decisions yet today' when the query errors (admin-a/approvals.tsx:383-386); the desktop topbar search form is a no-op (shell/topbar.tsx:84).
items.fix: In clearLocal() call queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: ['admin-b'] }) as well (or qc.clear()), or key admin queries by admin id. Add ['admin-b'] to the four-eyes refresh() invalidations.

items.title: Circuit-breaker e2e can leave pool.entries.enabled=false for good in the shared test DB, and the stuck state keeps itself going
items.scenario:
A run reaches the approved pause (line ~281, entriesEnabled:false), then the finally-block resume (lines 308-330) does not complete. This happens if vitest hits the 60 s testTimeout and afterAll closes the app under the still-running finally, if the run is killed, or if a resume call errors. feature_flags.pool.entries.enabled stays false in globalpool_test. On every later run the pause request at line 244 gets 409 'New entries are already paused' (admin-pool.service.ts:689). That happens before the try block, so the resume never runs and the flag stays off. Meanwhile every entry purchase in rounds/player/pool-history/rg-history/chain/openapi e2e gets 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE. Any other agent's concurrent run on the same DB also gets 503s during the paused window.
  EVIDENCE: Nothing resets feature flags: global-setup.ts only runs migrate deploy, and createTestApp/ensureRbac never touch feature_flags. The flag is persisted by upsert (admin-pool.service.ts:813). The test asserts isEnabled===true only after the request (line 256) and after the finally (line 331), so it never repairs state. If the pause was never applied, the finally's resume itself 409s ('already open') and hides the original failure.
items.fix: Restore state in an afterEach/afterAll that writes the flag directly (featureFlag.upsert enabled:true + FeatureFlagsService.invalidate()). Also reset it in global-setup. At the start of the test, if the flag is already false, restore it before requesting the pause. Don't do a dual-approval resume inside finally.

items.title: ensureRbac throws on any non-built-in admin role, and the role-change test leaks one when it fails
items.scenario:
admin-console 'roles & permissions ... need four eyes' creates role qa_xxxx (admin-console.e2e-spec.ts:469). It deletes it only on the last line (504), with no try/finally. If any assertion or TOTP step in between fails, the qa_ role stays in globalpool_test. From then on, every createAdmin() call in every e2e file runs ensureRbac. That does ROLE_PERMISSIONS[r.key].map(...) over prisma.adminRole.findMany() and throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading map)' for the qa_ row. So admin, admin-console, admin-ops, chain and rg-history all fail until someone deletes the row by hand. A concurrent run on the shared DB hits the same crash during the few seconds the role exists in a passing run.
  EVIDENCE: helpers.ts:145-153 maps every DB role through ROLE_PERMISSIONS with no guard. The test DB currently has 0 qa_ roles, so the suite is green only because the test has not failed between lines 469 and 504.
items.fix: In ensureRbac, filter roles to ADMIN_ROLES (or skip keys missing from ROLE_PERMISSIONS). Wrap the test role in try/finally (or afterAll) so it is always deleted.

items.title: The e2e global setup and db:migrate:test fall back to the dev DATABASE_URL when DATABASE_URL_TEST is unset
items.scenario:
A developer shell or .env has DATABASE_URL (globalpool) but no DATABASE_URL_TEST, for example an older .env or an exported variable. 'pnpm test' runs test/global-setup.ts, which spawns 'prisma.mjs migrate deploy --test-db'. Because DATABASE_URL_TEST is unset, env.mjs keeps DATABASE_URL, so pending (possibly WIP) migrations are applied to the shared dev DB. setup-env.ts:26-29 then points the tests at a hard-coded default globalpool_test that was never migrated, so the suite fails. Worse, the documented 'db:migrate:test' (package.json:21, docs/API.md:45 'reset the test database') runs 'migrate reset --force' and drops and recreates the shared dev database.
  EVIDENCE: env.mjs:13 only switches when GP_USE_TEST_DB==='1' AND DATABASE_URL_TEST is set, otherwise silently keeps DATABASE_URL. The '_test' safety regex exists only in setup-env.ts:30-31, which runs after global setup and never in the prisma wrapper.
items.fix: In prisma.mjs/env.mjs, when --test-db is passed: fail if DATABASE_URL_TEST is missing (or use the same default as setup-env), and refuse any URL whose database name does not end in _test before spawning prisma.

items.title: admin-a/admin-b Playwright specs reuse the shared DEMO admins at the current TOTP step: replay rejections and lockouts
items.scenario:
In one 'playwright test' run, admin-a.spec signs in k.osei at step S (admin-a.spec.ts:86-88), then submits an MFA code for S+1 (line 146), so totp_secrets.last_used_step = S+1. Under a minute later, admin-b.spec signs in the same k.osei with totpAt(timeStep()), which is S or S+1 (admin-b.spec.ts:97-98, 110). The API rejects it via afterTimeStep, the sign-in fails, and the test fails. Each rejected code adds to failedLoginAttempts. After ADMIN_LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 retries, the shared DEMO admin is locked for 15 min on the dev DB, which also blocks other agents. Other agents using the same DEMO admins cause the same rejection at random.
  EVIDENCE: _journey.ts:5-7 and :118-125 state that every step is accepted once per admin across agents, and pick max(now, last_used_step+1) from the DB. admin-a/admin-b signIn() ignores last_used_step. totp.service.ts:165-173 rejects any step <= lastUsedStep, and admin-auth.service.ts:84-93 counts it as a failed login.
items.fix: Reuse the _journey freshCode/adminCode helper (read last_used_step, wait for the next unused step) in admin-a.spec and admin-b.spec. Or give each spec its own seeded admin instead of the shared DEMO admins.

items.title: Odds disclosure rounds half-up, so disclosed chances are overstated
items.scenario:
oddsDisclosure(35, 18640) gives firstPrizePercent '0.188' (exact 0.187768...%), and oddsDisclosure(2, 3) gives firstPrizePercent '66.667' (exact 66.666...%); I reproduced both against the built dist. GET /pool/rounds/:id/my-entries calls it with the default 3 decimals (rounds.service.ts:171). The web approxPercent() rounds down, but it receives a value that was already rounded up, so the player sees '≈0.188%'. For values below 0.1% it shows 4 dp of a 3-dp half-up value: 1/1500 is shown as '≈0.0670%' against an exact 0.0666%. The hero shows anyPrizeApproxPercent without any further rounding (apps/web/src/components/home/hero.tsx:222,763).
  EVIDENCE: `const pct = (x: MoneyInput) => money(x).times(100).toDecimalPlaces(decimals).toFixed();`. No rounding mode is passed, so it uses MoneyDecimal's ROUND_HALF_UP (packages/shared/src/money.ts:22-27). The owner rule is that the odds disclosure rounds down.
items.fix: Use `toDecimalPlaces(decimals, Decimal.ROUND_DOWN)` in pct(). Have the API return at least 6 decimals so the web round-down is not applied to an already rounded value.

items.title: Withdraw 'MAX' button rounds the amount up, so the form errors with 'exceeds your available balance'
items.scenario:
Available is 100.005 USDT, which happens after a 6-dp on-chain deposit. The button reads 'MAX · 100.00' because formatUSDT truncates, but clicking it sets the amount to money('100.005').toFixed(2) = '100.01' because MoneyDecimal rounds half-up. `over` (gt(v, available)) becomes true and the step shows 'Exceeds your available balance (100.00 USDT)'. The MAX action never produces a valid amount.
  EVIDENCE: `onClick={() => onChange(money(max).toFixed(2))}` next to the label `MAX · {formatUSDT(max, { symbol: false })}`. MoneyDecimal is configured with rounding ROUND_HALF_UP (packages/shared/src/money.ts:22-27). Line 671: `const over = valid && gt(v, available);`.
items.fix: Use `roundDown(max, 2).toFixed(2)` (or pass `max` unrounded) so the filled amount never exceeds Available or the remaining daily limit. Left out, 2 lower-impact issues: the DEMO deposit-limit check in deposits.service.ts:211 and demo-deposits.service.ts:43 runs without a per-user lock, so concurrent simulations exceed the limit; and entries.service.ts:90-121 creates the entry_purchase transaction and posting without isDemo: round.isDemo, while the settlement and refund postings set it.

items.title: Admin login leaks a correct password (423 instead of the generic 401) while the admin's TOTP factor is locked, and reveals existing admin emails via the 403 lock response
items.scenario:
An admin mistypes 5 MFA codes on console actions, which locks the TOTP row for STEP_UP_LOCK_MINUTES=15. During that window a password-guessing attacker gets 401 'Invalid email, password or authenticator code' for wrong passwords. For the right password they get 423 STEP_UP_LOCKED 'Too many incorrect codes', because verifyRow throws before the generic path, and that attempt is not counted. Separately, 5 bad attempts against a candidate email return 403 'temporarily locked' only when the account exists; unknown emails always return 401. This enumerates admin emails and lets anyone lock any admin out.
  EVIDENCE: admin-auth.service.ts:78-82 calls `this.totp.verifyRow(...)` only when passwordOk. totp.service.ts:152-156 throws STEP_UP_LOCKED (mapped to 423) when row.lockedUntil > now, bypassing the INVALID message and the failed-attempt update at admin-auth.service.ts:84-97. Lines 67-72 return a distinct FORBIDDEN error for a locked existing account.
items.fix: In login, treat a locked TOTP factor as a plain failure (catch it and fall through to the generic 401 and counter update). Return the same generic 401 for locked accounts, or apply the lock uniformly by email hash.

items.title: AML alert resolution writes its audit row outside the action, so a failed audit append leaves a resolved alert with no audit trail
items.scenario:
A compliance admin dismisses an AML alert. aml.resolve() commits the status change on its own (aml.service.ts:100-108). The separate audit.record() call then fails, for example on an advisory-lock or hash-chain insert error or a DB blip. The client gets a 5xx, but the alert stays 'dismissed' with resolvedByAdminId set and no audit_logs row. Architecture requires sensitive actions to write their hash-chained audit row inside the same transaction.
  EVIDENCE: admin.controller.ts:291-309: assertSensitive, then `const alert = await this.aml.resolve(id, admin.id, …)` (default db = this.prisma, no tx), then `await this.audit.record({... action: 'aml.alert.resolved' ...})` with no tx argument. AmlService.resolve accepts a `db` parameter, but the controller does not pass a transaction. resolve() also has no status guard, so resolved or auto_rejected alerts can be re-resolved.
  ALSO REPORTED (fairness-admin): AML alert resolution writes its audit row in a separate transaction and can silently re-decide an already closed alert — Compliance admin C1 escalates alert X. Later, admin C2 calls POST /admin/aml/alerts/X/resolve with resolution 'dismissed'. AmlService.resolve does no status check, so it overwrites status, resolution text, resolvedAt and resolvedByAdminId, and the alert row no longer shows who escalated it. Separately, if audit.record fails after the update (e.g. advisory-lock wait exceeding maxWait 10 s), the alert stays resolved with no audit row. This contradicts 'write their hash-chained audit row inside the same transaction'.
items.fix: Wrap the resolve and the audit in this.prisma.tx(), passing tx to both aml.resolve(..., tx) and audit.record(..., tx). Add a status guard (only open/under_review/escalated may be resolved).

items.title: Compose 'prod' profile builds the web in DEV MOCK auth mode by default, so player sign-in is broken against the production API
items.scenario:
An operator follows the compose header: they set PRIVY_APP_ID and NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID in .env and run `docker compose --profile prod up --build`. The shared x-web build args pass NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_MOCK=${NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_MOCK:-true}, and .env.example also sets it to true, so publicEnv.privyMock is true even with an app id. AuthProvider mounts MockAuthProvider, which calls POST /auth/dev/token. The prod API (Privy mode) answers 404 'Cannot POST /auth/dev/token', so no player can sign in.
  EVIDENCE: docker-compose.yml:54-66 x-web args (used by both web and web-dev) with `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_MOCK: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_MOCK:-true}`. The Dockerfile web-build stage defaults ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_MOCK=true. apps/web/src/lib/env.ts:12 `privyMock: privyAppId === '' || process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_MOCK === 'true'`. auth-provider.tsx:21 uses MockAuthProvider when privyMock is true. auth.controller.ts:116 returns NOT_FOUND unless mode is 'mock'.
items.fix: Give the prod web service its own build args with NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_MOCK=false, and require a non-empty NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID there. Or make privyMock depend only on an empty app id outside development. Nothing else was left out: these 9 findings are all the defects found in this dimension.

items.title: Circuit-breaker request expiry is applied with an unguarded overwrite and no audit row, and approval is not re-checked against expiry inside the decision transaction
items.scenario:
A pause request P approaches its 30-minute TTL. Approver B passes the expiry check (line 792), verifies MFA, and commits 'approved' plus the flag change. Concurrently, admin C files a new request: C read P as pending before B's commit, considered it expired, and in its transaction runs `adminApproval.update({where:{id:P}, data:{status:'expired'}})` without a status predicate. This overwrites B's 'approved', so the breaker history shows the applied pause as 'expired', and no 'approval.expired' audit row is written. Separately, B's approval can commit after the TTL has passed, because the expiry is evaluated before MFA and not inside the transaction at 802.
  EVIDENCE: requestBreaker 692-705: existing is read outside the transaction, then `tx.adminApproval.update({ where: { id: existing.id }, data: { status: 'expired' } })` runs with no status guard and no audit.record. decideBreaker 792-800 checks the expiry outside the transaction, and the transaction claim at 802-811 filters only on status 'pending'. Left out of this report as minor or currently unreachable: 3 items. They are the DB-vs-contract winner-count divergence when entries are fewer than 13 (unreachable with the default 500-participant threshold), the per-process 15 s feature-flag cache delaying a breaker pause on other replicas, and the web verifier always stating the on-chain snapshot root is unpublished.
items.fix: Expire with updateMany({ where: { id, status: 'pending' } }) and record an 'approval.expired' system audit row when count === 1. In decideBreaker, add `createdAt > now - TTL` to the claiming updateMany predicate, or re-check the expiry inside the transaction after the claim.

items.title: Daily play-time and session-length limits rely only on client heartbeats; entry purchases never count as activity
items.scenario:
A player sets a 60-minute daily time limit, then buys entries straight through POST /pool/rounds/:id/entries (script, other client, or with the heartbeat request blocked). playedTodaySeconds and sessionStartedAt only move in heartbeat(), so timeBlock() never returns daily_time_limit or session_limit and the entries go through without limit.
  EVIDENCE: responsible-gaming.service.ts:466-475 is the only code that calls applyHeartbeat. assertTimeRules (:540-552) only reads those counters. entries.service.ts:78 calls assertCanParticipate but records no activity. The web sends heartbeats only from RealityCheckHost (reality-check.tsx:156-163), and only on play routes with recent input.
items.fix: Record activity on the server (applyHeartbeat-equivalent) inside the entry purchase (and future bet) transaction, so time accrues from server-observed play and does not depend on the client. Left out of this report: 2 more low findings. (1) restricted.tsx:298 says prizes go to Available, but they are posted to Owed and need a claim. (2) assertTimeRules reads the raw rg_settings row without applying due pending changes (stricter-only).

items.title: Hot-wallet liquidity race: concurrent withdrawals pass the balance check and the later one fails on-chain instead of staying queued
items.scenario:
The hot wallet holds 100 test-USDT and two 60 USDT withdrawals are queued. The withdrawals worker runs with concurrency 4, so both WITHDRAWAL_BROADCAST jobs read balanceOf=100 and simulate transfer() at 'latest' before either tx is mined. Both are signed with nonces N and N+1. The second reverts on-chain (ERC20InsufficientBalance), and after 20 confirmations it is marked 'failed' with 'token transfer reverted on-chain'. That contradicts the documented 'missing liquidity keeps the withdrawal queued, never silently failed', makes the player redo step-up 2FA, and wastes gas.
  EVIDENCE: Lines 80-95 read balanceOf/getBalance at latest state and ignore in-flight outbox rows from the same hot wallet. Lines 96-108 send. withdrawals.processor.ts:14 sets `concurrency: 4`. Lines 213-218 fail the withdrawal on a reverted receipt.
items.fix: Serialise hot-wallet sends (advisory lock), or subtract the sum of signed/broadcast-but-unmined withdrawal amounts from the balance before deciding. Treat an on-chain ERC20InsufficientBalance revert as 're-queue' rather than 'failed'. Two minor items were left out of this report: concurrent round-op step() sends across replicas, and dust deposits ignoring minDeposit.

items.title: Primary navigation (sidebar, mobile tab bar, footer, dashboard tabs, homepage) is full of links to unbuilt routes
items.scenario:
At 390 px, the bottom tab bar's 'Games' tab (/originals) always shows the 404 page. On desktop, the sidebar items Originals, all 5 game children, Casino games plus its 4 children, Winners, VIP Club, Affiliates, Promotions and Support all 404. The /dashboard sub-nav tabs 'VIP' (/vip) and 'Referrals' (/affiliates) 404, as do the homepage game tiles and 'All games' buttons.

Sidebar (nav-config.ts:75-133): /originals, /games/{orbit-rush,pool-dice,double-side,pool-roulette,twenty-one}, /casino, /casino/{table,slots,live,draws}, /winners, /vip, /affiliates, /promotions, /support. TAB_NAV games → /originals (line 140). Dashboard tabs: components/account/nav.ts:87-88 (/vip, /affiliates). Topbar mobile search: shell/topbar.tsx:97 (/search); the desktop search form only calls preventDefault (line 84). Gaming history: rg-history/gaming.tsx:161, 280 and 946 (/games/${slug}, /originals). Unkn
items.fix: Hide nav items whose route is not built (or render them disabled with 'Coming soon'), point the 'Games' tab at a page that exists, or add a (app)/[...slug] catch-all that renders an honest 'not built yet' state inside the shell, as admin does.

items.title: player.e2e and openapi.e2e leave an open under_review withdrawal behind on every run
items.scenario:
Each run of player.e2e (100.00 under_review, flagged, line 317) and openapi.e2e (50.00, openapi.e2e-spec.ts:131) leaves a withdrawal open forever in globalpool_test. The admin queue (oldest first) grows by 2+ per run. This is the root cause of the admin.e2e 'flagged withdrawals need FOUR EYES' failure once more than 20 were open. That test now works around it by reading the first and last page (admin.e2e-spec.ts:231-250), but the leak keeps going, and the queue SLA/summary aggregates in admin-ops and any future first-page assertion drift with test history.
  EVIDENCE: wallet.e2e-spec.ts:291-292 already cancels its withdrawal with the comment 'Leave no open review behind in the shared test database'. player and openapi do not. A read-only count in globalpool_test shows 51 under_review withdrawals (21 created in the 05:00 hour alone).
items.fix: POST /withdrawals/:id/cancel at the end of both tests (or in afterAll), as wallet.e2e does.

items.title: sanitizeAmount reads ',' as a decimal point, and a unit test locks that in, so pasted amounts lose their thousands
items.scenario:
The app shows amounts with comma thousands separators (Amount renders '9,215.30'; the AmountInput header shows 'Available 9,215.30 USDT'). A player pastes 9,215.30 into the withdraw amount and gets 9.21. Typing '1,000' as a deposit or participation limit in limit-setter.tsx:143/279 gives 1.00. The deposit-flow amount (deposit-flow.tsx:647/787) does the same.
  EVIDENCE: raw.replace(/,/g,'.') runs before the dot split, so '1,234.50' becomes '1.234.50' and then '1.23'. apps/web/test/logic.test.ts:13 asserts sanitizeAmount('1,234.5', 2) === '1.23', so the test enshrines the wrong result instead of catching it.
items.fix: Strip ',' when the string also contains '.', or when ',' is followed by exactly 3 digits (thousands grouping). Only treat a lone ',' as a decimal point. Update logic.test.ts to expect '1234.50'.

items.title: CI never uses the Foundry 'ci' profile, so contracts get 1,024 fuzz runs and 64 invariant runs instead of 10,000 and 512
items.scenario:
foundry.toml defines [profile.ci.fuzz] runs=10_000 and [profile.ci.invariant] runs=512. The workflow's env block has no FOUNDRY_PROFILE, and the @gp/contracts test script runs a plain 'forge test'. So CI runs the default profile (fuzz 1,024, invariant 64x256), and the stronger CI fuzzing of the draw/settlement invariants never runs anywhere.
  EVIDENCE: grep finds no FOUNDRY_PROFILE in .github/workflows/global-pool-ci.yml or packages/contracts/package.json. The test step is 'pnpm -r test', which runs 'sh scripts/forge.sh test'.
items.fix: Set FOUNDRY_PROFILE: ci in the workflow env (or on the Test step), or add a 'test:ci' script that passes --profile ci and call it from CI.
